requirement: P4 publish every model total twice (two estimators, gap column) until one wins walk-forward
label: backtest corpus — not a leaderboard result

registration.rule: the commit that created the file is the registration; written here by a later commit

T1.name: prior-season pace fit
T1.definition: ridge least squares on six prior seasons; level + pace_home + pace_away

T2.name: league mean plus one third of the form gap
T2.implemented_in: skill-lab/scripts/build.py shrink_total() rule, applied to points-for/allowed

numbers.C5_min_n: 28 scored validation games against a floor of 20

decision.state: not collapsed: both estimators stay published with the gap column

diagnosis.reading: T2 prices 7.46 points below the realised total on average, while T1's bias is -0.11. Subtracting that constant only takes T2 from MAE 12.67 to 11.59, so the bias is not the whole story: T2's prediction spread is 0.67 points against a realised spread of 14.33, and its correlation with the realised total is 0.055 against 0.172 for T1. An estimator that varies by under a point cannot track a target that varies by fourteen. The cause is mechanical and is stated in the flagged table rather than repaired here: the registered T2 rule shrinks a mean of points-for and points-allowed toward a league level, and that mean sits near the league level by construction. Repairing it would be a new estimator, which the registration forbids after the fact.

inputs.note: computed from the published per-game columns on rows.html; no new estimator is introduced

flags.title: One corpus game has no published final score
flags.detail: 1 corpus row(s) — WAS at DAL (week 2) — carry blank score cells on the official page. The row is published with both estimator values and a blank truth, and is excluded from every score. It is not inferred.

flags.title: Estimator inputs are community data, the scored truth is official
flags.detail: T1's fit window and T2's rolling form both read the digest-verified community schedule snapshot (data/raw/games.csv, SHA-256 in data/raw/manifest.json). The comparison is therefore a comparison of two estimators on community inputs, scored against official finals. It is labelled that way on every page and is excluded from any official-only gate.

flags.title: The registered T2 rule is mechanically centred on the league level
flags.detail: T2 shrinks a mean of points-for and points-allowed (which is itself ≈ league level) toward the league level, so its prediction spread is 0.67 points. It loses to T1 on every pre-registered condition. Fixing it would mean registering a new estimator; this session does not do that after seeing the result.

flags.title: Sign convention in the T2 form mean is not stated by the source code
flags.detail: The registered skill-lab rule averages points-for and points-allowed together. If the intent were an expected total, points-allowed should carry the opposite sign to the opponent's points-for. The repository's code and its pre-registration agree with each other but neither states the intent, so this workspace reproduces the code as written and flags the ambiguity for the owner instead of choosing an interpretation.

flags.title: Corpus registration hash is self-referential in the manifest
flags.detail: corpus/manifest.json records corpus_registration as the commit that created its own pre-registration file, which cannot be known at the moment that file is created. The value is therefore a forward reference written by a later commit. This workspace verifies the corpus file hash instead, and does not treat the recorded hash as proof of ordering.

flags.title: One season, nine weeks, 135 scored games
flags.detail: The collapse decision is made on 28 validation games. That is above the frozen floor of 20 but small: a single 60-point game moves the mean absolute error by roughly a point. The interval, not the point estimate, is the published statistic.

flags.title: Nothing here is a price, an edge, ROI or a leaderboard result
flags.detail: The price firewall is closed at zero licensed sources, so no ROI, CLV or staking number is computable from this workspace by rule. The comparison is between two models on official final totals and carries no market claim.

questions.question: Should T2 be re-registered as an expected-total estimator with an explicit sign convention?
questions.known: The registered rule and its code agree; both shrink a mean of points-for and points-allowed.
questions.missing: A statement of intent from the owner: is the form term meant to be an expected total?
questions.route: Register T2b in a new commit, then re-run; the current pair stays published meanwhile.

questions.question: Does the pair hold up on a second season?
questions.known: 135 scored games from one season; T1 wins on all four failing conditions.
questions.missing: A frozen corpus for any other season, verified against official finals.
questions.route: Freeze 2025 the same way 2026 was frozen, then re-run this build unchanged.

questions.question: Should the league level be estimated from a rolling window rather than the train block?
questions.known: The level is 46.17 points from 93 training games, frozen before validation.
questions.missing: A pre-registered rule for refitting the level forward, and a decision on whether that is a new estimator.
questions.route: Write the rule as T2b before looking at any later week; it cannot be adopted retrospectively.

questions.question: Can either estimator be scored against a market total?
questions.known: A community total line exists for most 2026 games; the price policy excludes it from any published number.
questions.missing: One licensed price source with a named permitted use and both timestamps.
questions.route: Satisfy pricing/PRICE_DATA_POLICY.md §4; until then the market column stays blank.

questions.question: Is the club-code join ('AZ' → 'ARI') the only alias this corpus needs?
questions.known: The repository's audited cross-check matched 136/136 official finals using exactly this one mapping, and this workspace joined 136/136 rows with it.
questions.missing: Nothing for 2026. A future season could introduce another rendering difference.
questions.route: The next freeze records any new alias in its own pre-registration before use.

leakage.rule: PRE_REGISTRATION.md §3: every rolling input strictly earlier than the fixture kickoff date
leakage.t1_note: T1 is fitted on seasons s-6..s-1 only; no 2026 game enters any 2026 fit

determinism: no wall-clock value is recorded in this artifact; a rebuild from the committed inputs must be byte-identical, which two-total/scripts/verify.py enforces
